question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.5$ | $0$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$

current_example.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.4$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X, Y] = \sum_{(x,y)\in S}(x − \textrm E[X])(y − \textrm E[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $f_X$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ | $0.6$ |
| $X=2$ | $0$ | $0.4$ | $0.4$ |
| $f_Y$ | $0.1$ | $0.9$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\textrm{E}[X]$ and $\textrm{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.6+2\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.6+0.8 \\  & =1.4 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.9 \\  & =0+0.9 \\  & =0.9\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-1.4)(y-0.9)f(x,y) \\  & =(1-1.4)(0-0.9)f(1,0) \\  & +(1-1.4)(1-0.9)f(1,1) \\  & +(2-1.4)(0-0.9)f(2,0) \\  & +(2-1.4)(1-0.9)f(2,1) \\  & =(-0.4)(-0.9)(0.1) \\  & +(-0.4)(0.1)(0.5) \\  & +(0.6)(-0.9)(0) \\  & +(0.6)(0.1)(0.4) \\  & =0.04.\end{aligned}
$$
